full_name: Randomized Accelerated Proximal-Point Method (RapGrad) for Nonconvex Finite-Sum Optimization
source_reference: Lan, First-order and Stochastic Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Springer 2020 (Theorem 6.16)

problem.description: Nonconvex finite-sum minimization over a closed convex set.

variable_space.math: X\subseteq \mathbb{R}^n\text{ is a closed convex set, and }f_i:X\to\mathbb{R},\ i=1,\ldots,m,\text{ are nonconvex smooth functions}

assumptions.name: OptimalSolutions_Theorem6_16
assumptions.math: x^*\text{ and }x_\ell^*\text{ denote the optimal solutions to problem (6.6.1) and the }\ell\text{-th subproblem (6.6.7), respectively}.

main_theorem.statement_math: \text{Let the iterates }\bar{x}^\ell,\ \ell=1,\ldots,k,\text{ be generated by Algorithm 6.8 and }\hat{\ell}\text{ be randomly selected from }[k].\text{ Suppose that in Algorithm 6.9, }s=\left\lceil-\frac{\log M_F}{\log\alpha}\right\rceil\text{ with }M_F:=6\left(5+\frac{2L}{\mu}\right)\max\left\{\frac{6}{5},\frac{L^2}{\mu^2}\right\},\ \alpha=1-\frac{2}{m(\sqrt{1+16c/m}+1)},\ c=2+\frac{L}{\mu},\text{ and }\alpha_t=\alpha,\ \gamma_t=\alpha^{-t},\ \tau_t=\frac{1}{m(1-\alpha)}-1,\ \eta_t=\frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha},\ \forall t=1,\ldots,s.\text{ Then }\mathbb{E}\left[d\left(\nabla f(x_{\hat{\ell}}^*),-N_X(x_{\hat{\ell}}^*)\right)^2\right]\le\frac{36\mu}{k}\left[f(\bar{x}^0)-f(x^*)\right],\quad \mathbb{E}\|\bar{x}^{\hat{\ell}}-x_{\hat{\ell}}^*\|^2\le\frac{4\mu}{kL^2}\left[f(\bar{x}^0)-f(x^*)\right].
main_theorem.rate: The stationarity residual is O(mu [f(xbar0)-f(x*)]/k), and the distance from the reported iterate to the exact proximal subproblem solution is O(mu [f(xbar0)-f(x*)]/(k L^2)).
main_theorem.measure: Expected squared normal-cone stationarity defect at the exact solution of the randomly selected proximal subproblem, and expected squared distance between the computable random outer iterate and that exact solution.

key_lemmas.name: Lemma6_13_WeightedRaGradRecursion
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let the iterates }x^t\text{ and }y^t,\ t=1,\ldots,s,\text{ be generated by Algorithm 6.9 and }x^*\text{ be an optimal solution of (6.6.8). If the parameters in Algorithm 6.9 satisfy for all }t=1,\ldots,s-1,\ \alpha_{t+1}\gamma_{t+1}=\gamma_t,\ \gamma_{t+1}[m(1+\tau_{t+1})-1]\le m\gamma_t(1+\tau_t),\ \gamma_{t+1}\eta_{t+1}\le\gamma_t(1+\eta_t),\ \frac{\eta_s\mu}{4}\ge\frac{(m-1)^2\hat{L}}{m^2\tau_s},\ \frac{\eta_t\mu}{2}\ge\frac{\alpha_{t+1}\hat{L}}{\tau_{t+1}}+\frac{(m-1)^2\hat{L}}{m^2\tau_t},\ \frac{\eta_s\mu}{4}\ge\frac{\hat{L}}{m(1+\tau_s)},\text{ then }\mathbb{E}_s\left[\gamma_s(1+\eta_s)V_\varphi(x^*,x^s)+\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{\mu\gamma_s(1+\tau_s)}{4}\|x_i^s-x^*\|^2\right]\le\gamma_1\eta_1\mathbb{E}_sV_\varphi(x^*,x^0)+\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{\gamma_1[(1+\tau_1)-1/m]\hat{L}}{2}\mathbb{E}_s\|x_i^0-x^*\|^2.

key_lemmas.name: Theorem6_17_RaGradLinearContraction
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let }x^*\text{ be an optimal solution of (6.6.8), and suppose that the parameters }\{\alpha_t\},\{\tau_t\},\{\eta_t\},\text{ and }\{\gamma_t\}\text{ are set as in (6.6.16) and (6.6.17). If }\varphi(x)=\frac{\mu}{2}\|x-z\|^2,\text{ for some }z\in X,\text{ then, for any }s\ge1,\text{ we have }\mathbb{E}_s\|x^*-x^s\|^2\le\alpha^s\left(1+2\frac{\hat{L}}{\mu}\right)\mathbb{E}_s\left[\|x^*-x^0\|^2+\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m\|x_i^0-x^0\|^2\right],\quad \mathbb{E}_s\left[\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m\|x_i^s-x^s\|^2\right]\le6\alpha^s\left(1+2\frac{\hat{L}}{\mu}\right)\mathbb{E}_s\left[\|x^*-x^0\|^2+\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m\|x_i^0-x^0\|^2\right].

Also let the iterates }\bar{x}^\ell,\ \ell=1,\ldots,k,\text{ be generated by Algorithm 6.8, and }\hat{\ell}\text{ be randomly selected from }[k].\text{ Then }\mathbb{E}\|x_{\hat{\ell}}^*-\bar{x}^{\hat{\ell}-1}\|^2\le\frac{4(1-M\alpha^s)}{k\mu(6-7M\alpha^s)}[f(\bar{x}^0)-f(x^*)],\quad \mathbb{E}\|x_{\hat{\ell}}^*-\bar{x}^{\hat{\ell}}\|^2\le\frac{2M\alpha^s}{3k\mu(6-7M\alpha^s)}[f(\bar{x}^0)-f(x^*)].
